verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents its own isolation features. Tool execution can run inside a sandbox backend with modes, scopes and workspace access controls, and Docker is offered as an isolated, throwaway Gateway environment. Isolated agents and fleet cells also each get their own state, credentials and workspace, so you can try things in a separate environment rather than against your real setup. However, none of this is framed as a test or staging environment kept apart from production data, and how deep the sandbox's data separation goes is not shown. missing for 10: an explicit documented test/staging mode separated from production data, guidance on non-production credentials or data, independent or hands-on corroboration of sandbox isolation.
